Evidence is conflicting: a May 2026 report described Capesize rates rising on demand and tightening vessel supply, while an August 2026 BIMCO warning characterized apparent 2026 strength as substantially driven by forced rerouting and warned of a prospective supply glut. Current exact-driver persistence is therefore unresolved.

supporting_evidence.claim: A key dry-bulk freight-rate measure reached its highest level since December 2023, driven by rising Capesize demand and tightening ship supply.
supporting_evidence.source_title: Dry-Bulk Shipping Rates Hit Two-Year High on Capesize Demand

counter_evidence.claim: BIMCO warned that apparent 2026 dry-bulk strength was substantially artificial because of forced rerouting and that the market faced a future supply glut as the rerouting effect reversed.
counter_evidence.source_title: Dry bulk shipping faces 2027 supply glut: BIMCO warns Hormuz rerouting boost will reverse
